namingPolicyNotHistory: Korean map labels are editorial conventions; they do not change local official names, historical officialPeriods or the place identity.

boundary.description: Apply Korean Sino-Korean character readings for Chinese-language mainland toponyms before the 1912-01-01 founding of the Republic of China and a Chinese-pronunciation-based Korean map label from that date. This is a uniform PandoEditor editorial style change, not a city renaming or an assertion that Korean speakers immediately changed usage.
boundary.event: Founding of the Republic of China / 중화민국 건국 (1912-01-01)
boundary.geographicScope: Mainland China, for the selected Chinese-language local toponym; Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan are not automatically included.

rules.koreanLabelConvention: Korean transcription of Japanese place-name pronunciation
rules.exclude: Sino-Korean readings of Japanese place-name kanji as separate aliases (e.g. 동경 for 東京, 대판 for 大阪).
rules.historicalLocalToponyms: Respect actual historical name changes (e.g. 江戸 -> 에도, 東京 -> 도쿄).

rules.koreanLabelConvention: Sino-Korean reading of the date-appropriate selected Chinese-language local toponym
Korean rendering of Chinese pronunciation of the date-appropriate selected Chinese-language local toponym

resolutionOrder: For each map date, determine the established local city name and naming practice under sustained civil administration. Military occupation, temporary wartime rule and shifting front lines do not automatically replace that name with the occupier's language. Document a lasting territorial/legal change before reconsidering official language or name.
Match the Korean label to that selected period-appropriate native toponym; do not apply a reading of a different city's name or a different historical official name.
First resolve actual local-city-name changes for the map date. Never turn a Korean map-transcription convention change into an asserted Chinese official rename.
Choose the locally attested name from period-preferred historical entries, not any arbitrary names[] alias or extra spelling; year-only dates remain approximate.
Apply a map-label language convention to THAT toponym, not to its present-day English name.
Use a verified koMapLabels mapping if the name is covered; otherwise hold for review rather than guessing a transliteration.
Do not derive naming language, polity or sovereignty from sourceCountryCode; this is GeoNames source metadata only.
Only one preferred Korean display name may be selected at a given date. Do not keep historical Sino-Korean readings as concurrent alternate Korean map labels after the 1912-01-01 boundary.

Do not store short forms, nicknames, redundant romanizations, search-only aliases or occupying-power exonyms unless a form is explicitly selected as the preferred historical map name for an evidenced period. Maintain independent ko/en/native selection.
exceptions: For non-Mandarin Chinese-language varieties, minority-language and multilingual mainland localities, explicitly select the period's applicable local toponym and pronunciation; never infer Mandarin or sovereignty solely from a modern GeoNames CN country code. Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan are outside the automatic mainland rule and require separate consideration.
note: Chinese mainland Korean map pronunciation changes at 1912-01-01 are editorial, not legal city renamings. The global no-alias and temporary-occupation naming rules apply to ongoing batch reviews; already staged data elsewhere may need targeted cleanup. Runtime/place tiles are not changed by this policy update.

occupationAndAliasRule.militaryOccupation: Do not switch a Chinese or other local native name to the temporary occupier's language solely because an army controls the city; use sustained local naming and documented official changes.
occupationAndAliasRule.formalTransfer: A durable legal territorial transfer can prompt a review of local official language and naming, without itself mandating a new name.
occupationAndAliasRule.actualRenaming: Documented formal renaming is evaluated separately even during wartime; an occupation exonym with no lasting locally selected status is not an automatic preferred name.
occupationAndAliasRule.aliasRetention: No auxiliary aliases, unused transliterations, abbreviations or search-only records in names[]; previously selected historical preferred names remain valid for their dated periods.
